claim: The KiCad schematic editor provides a symbolic representation of circuit components and logical pin connections.
excerpt: The schematic is a symbolic representation of the circuit: which components are used and what connections are made between them.

claim: KiCad schematic workflows transfer component definitions and net connection information directly into the board editor.
excerpt: When the schematic is complete and the design has passed an electrical rules check (ERC), the design information in the schematic is transferred to the board editor and layout begins.

claim: KiCad PCB editor supports up to 32 copper layers and 14 technical layers including solder mask and silkscreen.
excerpt: KiCad is capable of creating printed circuit boards with up to 32 copper layers, 14 technical layers (silkscreen, solder mask, component adhesive, solder paste, etc), and 13 general-purpose drawing layers.

claim: KiCad design rule settings define clearance values, track widths, and via sizes per netclass prior to routing.
excerpt: Every class has values for copper clearance, track width, via sizes, and differential pair sizes.

claim: Freerouting processes Specctra DSN input files from CAD tools and exports routed Specctra SES session files.
excerpt: Freerouting is an advanced autorouter for all PCB programs that support the standard Specctra or Electra DSN interface. It imports `.dsn` files generated by your CAD software and exports routed `.ses` session files.

claim: Specctra DSN format exports routing information and design constraints from KiCad to external autorouting tools.
excerpt: The Specctra DSN exporter creates a file suitable for importing into certain third-party autorouter software.

claim: Copper zones define solid or hatched copper areas attached to specific electrical nets on PCB layers.
excerpt: Copper zones, also sometimes called copper pours or fills by other EDA tools, are solid or hatched areas of copper assigned to a particular net

claim: Thermal relief spokes regulate copper width when pads connect to surrounding copper zones to ease soldering.
excerpt: Thermal relief spoke width controls the width of the spokes generated when the zone connection mode is Thermal Relief.

claim: Electrical rules checks automatically detect incorrect or missing connections at the schematic capture level.
excerpt: Electrical rules check (ERC) for the automatic control of incorrect and missing connections

claim: Design rules checks verify physical board layout constraints prior to generating manufacturing fabrication outputs.
excerpt: When the board layout is complete and the board has passed the Design Rules Check (DRC), fabrication outputs are generated so that the board can be manufactured by a PCB fabricator.

claim: KiCad generates CNC drill files for board fabrication in Excellon or Gerber X2 formats.
excerpt: Choose whether to generate Excellon drill files (required by most PCB manufacturers) or Gerber X2 files.

claim: KiCad produces component placement files in POS format to specify footprint placement and rotation for assembly.
excerpt: To create placement files, select Component Placement (.pos, .gbr)… from the Fabrication Outputs section of the File menu.

claim: The open source marbastlib library provides MX and Choc switch footprints and parts for custom keyboard PCB design.
excerpt: A library collecting MX and Choc style footprints, as well as various other parts used to design custom keyboards

claim: The keyboard-pcb-guide repository serves as a community reference for designing keyboard PCBs using KiCad.
excerpt: Guide on how to design keyboard PCBs with KiCad.
